title: academy-messages/v1
description: The lock screen's SYSTEM BROADCAST feed. Governs the two Workers KV values (messages:ops, messages:manual) that functions/messages.json.ts merges, the scripts/seed-messages.json seed, and every payload written through PUT /api/messages.

message.$comment: Every field is required. There is no message worth broadcasting that lacks any one of them, and an omitted field only ever means the author forgot.

id.description: Stable and unique within its key. An id in messages:ops shadows the same id in messages:manual, which is how an incident is resolved: rewrite the entry in place rather than stacking a second one beside it.

level.description: Drives the dot and tag colour: update=cyan, info=gray, alert=amber, resolved=green. `alert` also PINS the message to the top of the panel, above every other level, regardless of date. `resolved` does not pin — it falls back to date order, so a resolved incident ages out naturally.

date.description: REQUIRED. `YYYY-MM-DD`, or a full ISO 8601 datetime when the writer has one (a health check does). ISO strings compare lexicographically in chronological order, so a timestamp orders correctly against a bare date on the same day. Only the first 10 characters are rendered.
date.$comment: A `pattern`, not `format: date`, so this schema compiles to a standalone validator with no ajv-formats dependency: the Workers runtime forbids `new Function`, so PUT /api/messages imports code generated ahead of time by scripts/build-validator.mjs. The ranges are spelled out rather than left as \d{2} so the regex still rejects month 13 and day 45, which is what a typo actually looks like. It does not know how long February is; that is the one gap accepted in exchange for keeping the schema the single source of truth, with no second check to drift from it.
